title: review: C-O2a: host-portable account auth and role secrets — oauth_token_env per Claude account, env:NAME secret values
spec: Why: on a headless Linux host the Claude accounts authenticate with long-lived tokens (`claude setup-token` → CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, one per CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and role secrets cannot come from the laptop's `f tok get` Keychain wrapper (pool.toml [secrets.*], spawn.py:78-85 secrets_for_role). (1) pool.py: [[claude_accounts]] gains optional `oauth_token_env` (string); Account exposes it. (2) spawn.py run_claude: when the picked account has oauth_token_env and that variable is set in the environment, put its value into the child env as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; never log it. (3) spawn.py secrets_for_role: a value of the form `env:NAME` reads os.environ[NAME] (missing → skip with a stderr note naming NAME, not the value); any other value keeps today's shell-command behaviour. (4) pool.toml: comment the two forms next to [secrets.scout]; do not change the current values (the laptop still uses the command form). (5) README.md: a short "Headless hosts" paragraph pointing at the two options. Tests in tests/test_spawn.py: env form is read; missing env var is skipped without raising; command form unchanged; run_claude env contains CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when configured and set, and lacks it otherwise (patch subprocess.Popen with the harness FakeProc pattern).
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py gains tests for env-form secrets (present, missing) and for CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN injection (configured+set, configured+unset, not configured); all green
A pool.toml without oauth_token_env and with today's command-form secrets behaves exactly as before (existing tests untouched and green)
No token value appears in any log line or bus record (grep the diff for print/log of the value)
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency
